verses.text: That night the king could not sleep. So he ordered the book of records to be brought and read to him.
It was found written there how Mordecai had told about Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king's officials who guarded the door, who had planned to kill King Xerxes.
The king asked, "What honor and reward was given to Mordecai for this?" The king's servants who were with him answered, "Nothing has been done for him."
The king asked, "Who is in the courtyard?" Haman had just come into the outer courtyard of the palace to ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on the pole he had set up for him.
The king's servants told him, "Haman is standing in the courtyard." The king said, "Let him come in."
When Haman came in, the king asked him, "What should be done for the man the king wants to honor?" Haman thought to himself, "Who would the king want to honor more than me?"
So he answered the king, "For the man the king wants to honor,
let them bring a royal robe the king has worn, and a horse the king has ridden, with a royal crown on its head.

Let the robe and the horse be given to one of the king's most important officials. Let him dress the man the king wants to honor, lead him on the horse through the city square, and shout ahead of him, 'This is what is done for the man the king wants to honor!'"
The king said to Haman, "Hurry. Take the robe and the horse, just as you said, and do this for Mordecai the Jew, who sits at the king's gate. Do not leave out anything you have said."
So Haman took the robe and the horse. He dressed Mordecai and led him on the horse through the city square, shouting ahead of him, "This is what is done for the man the king wants to honor!"
Afterward Mordecai went back to the king's gate. But Haman hurried home, sad and covering his head in shame.

Haman told his wife Zeresh and all his friends everything that had happened to him. His wise advisers and his wife Zeresh said to him, "You have started to fall before Mordecai. Since he is a Jew, you cannot win against him. You will surely be ruined."
While they were still talking with him, the king's officials arrived and hurried Haman off to the dinner Esther had prepared.
